summary: The candidate is a substantive partial fix: configured LRU eviction bounds real PUSH/monitor descriptor growth and its cleanup tests pass, but the fixed default cache size of 1024 can exceed the process FD budget. With RLIMIT_NOFILE=128, the unchanged candidate still raises the original ZMQError after 32 endpoints; manually configuring the cache to 8 survives 1,000 endpoints.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual CommonKVManager._connect with real PyZMQ retained 200 socket and 200 monitor entries; /proc/self/fd grew from 9 to 613, peak 614.
All five candidate regressions passed against source imported from /job/repo/python, covering bounded/LRU caching, paired closure, reuse, busy-socket handling, and monitor-creation cleanup.
Actual CommonKVManager._connect with real PyZMQ ended after 200 endpoints with 8 socket and 8 monitor entries; /proc/self/fd grew from 9 to 45, peak 48.
The probe caught zmq.error.ZMQError: Too many open files after 32 successfully created endpoints, before the 1024-entry eviction threshold.
The same real path completed 1,000 unique endpoints without error, ending with 8 cached entries and 38 descriptors, proving the LRU mechanism works when sized to the process budget.
376 tests passed with 47 subtests; no focused-suite compatibility regression was observed.

remaining_counterexamples: With the candidate default SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ZMQ_SOCKET_CACHE_SIZE=1024 and a per-process soft RLIMIT_NOFILE of 128, real CommonKVManager._connect raises ZMQError: Too many open files after 32 endpoints, before eviction can occur.

The fix requires operators with lower descriptor budgets to discover and manually tune the new cache-size environment variable; the default is not derived from RLIMIT_NOFILE or current descriptor headroom.
remaining_limitations: The reporter's 16x NVIDIA H800 full-model and multi-node serving workload was unavailable; only the actual host-side CommonKVManager/PyZMQ path was reproduced.
The assigned device was one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. No GPU execution was relevant to the descriptor lifecycle and none was claimed.
No native source changed and repository-environment.json reports native as null, so no native rebuild was applicable.

On the reporter's stated soft limit of 1,048,576, the candidate's default 1024-entry bound is expected to prevent this cache alone from exhausting descriptors, but the unavailable distributed workload was not reproduced.
